# Monier-Williams — Sanskrit-English Dictionary (1899), enumeration entries

## Identity, selected edition and historical scope

Monier Monier-Williams, *A Sanskrit-English Dictionary* (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1899), selected Cologne Digital Sanskrit Lexicon transcriptions, printed-page locators 1128.1 and 1199.1. The complete returned entry groups were read. The printed-page numbers are reported by Cologne; this admission does not claim a fresh scan collation. The Merriam-Webster house is a different dictionary and supplies no Sanskrit authority.

The lexical relation is within Sanskrit: saṃ-√khyā, saṃkhyā and sāṃkhya. The entry gives alternative explanations for the philosophical name and historical opinions characteristic of its edition. Those opinions are not silently promoted into current consensus. The case uses the primary Kārikā to establish its actual classification rather than reconstructing the system from the dictionary’s compressed list.

## Passages and excerpts

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p001"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p001 — Counting and an articulated number

**Paraphrase:** The saṃ-√khyā entry includes reckoning, counting up, enumeration and calculation. The feminine noun saṃkhyā includes numeration, a total, a numeral and grammatical number; it also records deliberation and an appellation as distinct senses. The several senses do not establish one original practice or license transferring every sense into every occurrence.

- **Locator:** Cologne entry group saMKyA; printed p.1128, col.1; IDs 228400 and 228407–228415.
- **Verification:** Read against the saved selected carrier on 2026-09-08; English explanation is a paraphrase, not a claimed transcription.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Status:** citation-ready for the scoped online passage; no exact quotation admitted.
- **Use boundary:** Lexical range only. Its cited Sanskrit works have not all been read. No relation of descent to English account or Hebrew SPR is asserted.

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p002"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p002 — The philosophical name

**Paraphrase:** The sāṃkhya entry records numerical and discriminative uses and the name of the philosophical school. It offers discrimination or, more probably in its own wording, enumeration of twenty-five tattvas as explanations of that name. This is a lexicographer’s qualified explanation, not a dated declaration by the school’s founder.

- **Locator:** Cologne sAMKya; printed p.1199, col.1; IDs 241218–241225, especially 241225.
- **Verification:** Read against the saved selected carrier on 2026-09-08; English explanation is a paraphrase, not a claimed transcription.
- **Source relation:** Paraphrased.
- **Status:** citation-ready for the scoped online passage; no exact quotation admitted.
- **Use boundary:** Retain the alternative explanations and their uncertainty. The independent primary passage establishes the classification; lexical derivation does not prove its ontology.


## Further selected online witnesses — formation and differentiation

Five complete returned Cologne entry groups were read on 2 October 2026. These add a selected lexical witness to the original enumeration admission; they do not change the source’s original access date, print or exact-quotation standing. The original two enumeration cards remain intact. Their reported page and column numbers and the following locators belong to the Cologne transcription, not a fresh collation of page images.

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p003"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p003 — kḷp: selected formative entry

**Paraphrase:** kḷp has senses of being suitably related, ordered, adapted or fit, and of preparing, producing and considering as. Its causative includes arranging, distributing, making, framing, imagining and, in particular uses, trimming or cutting. A formative root does not by itself guarantee a revisable arrangement or exclude every cutting sense.

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p004"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p004 — vi-: selected formative entry

**Paraphrase:** The third vi entry is the prefix or indeclinable, distinct from the bird and artificial-word homonyms in the returned group. It includes separation, different directions, division, distinction, distribution, arrangement, order, opposition and deliberation. The entry treats an original dvi, in the sense of two parts, as probable. The prefix can also intensify, negate or leave a root’s meaning largely unmodified.

- **Locator:** Cologne entry group `vi`; reported printed p.949, col.3; ID192832 and192832.1–4.
- **Carrier:** [Official selected Cologne entry](https://www.sanskrit-lexicon.uni-koeln.de/scans/MWScan/2020/web/webtc/getword.php?key=vi&filter=roman&transLit=slp1); retained HTML `working/canonical-argument-recovery-2026-09-25/foundation-closure-2026-10-01/concept-legacy-operation-return/source-objects/mw-vi.html.txt`, SHA-256 `ed563f508ea2e1f2050a0146de093b4a867adcfb15116ae9832ee36306d4ae89`; rendered entry text `working/canonical-argument-recovery-2026-09-25/foundation-closure-2026-10-01/concept-legacy-operation-return/source-objects/mw-vi-text.txt`, SHA-256 `3362b7004bedb5affc7b6b62a58d23c3f5f759d0fd780b4dc48257c01e2b9a23`.

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p005"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p005 — sam-: selected formative entry

**Paraphrase:** The second sam entry is the prefix or indeclinable, distinct from the verbal root in the same returned group. It includes togetherness, conjunction, union, thoroughness, intensity and completeness, and is placed in opposition to the third vi. Its examples include intensified destruction as well as joining.

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p006"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p006 — vikalpa: selected formative entry

**Paraphrase:** The second vi-kalpa includes alternative or option, variation, combination and diversity, contrivance, perceptual distinction, doubt, admission or statement, false notion or imagination, calculation, thinking, rhetorical antithesis and grammatical optionality. The returned group also distinguishes an intermediate kalpa under the first entry.

<a id="monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p007"></a>
### monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p007 — saṃkalpa: selected formative entry

**Paraphrase:** Saṃ-kalpa includes an idea or conception formed in mind or heart, will, desire, purpose, definite intention, determination or decision, conviction and expectation. It also gives a ritual declaration of purpose and personified or named uses, which remain distinguishable from the ordinary mental and intentional senses.
